habitat: Flocks stay with buffalo, rhinoceros, domestic cattle and donkeys, clinging on while they search the coat.
summary: A fairly common, localised oxpecker. The head and upperparts are dark brown, the underparts and rump are yellow-buff, and the heavy bill is yellow with a red tip. The eye is yellow. The tail is longer than the Red-billed Oxpecker’s, and the rump and upper tail coverts are pale. The immature has a dusky brown bill and is duller. The call is a hissing kuss, kuss, higher than the Red-billed Oxpecker.

similar.note: Red-billed Oxpecker has an entirely red bill, a large yellow eye-wattle and no pale rump. Yellow-billed Oxpecker has the heavy yellow bill with a red tip, a pale rump and a longer tail.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^9=512 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 256–1024.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

viewNotes.note: Heavy yellow bill with a red tip, dark brown head and a pale rump, usually on a large mammal.
The yellow-and-red bill and yellow eye are the front marks.
Pale rump and upper tail coverts, and a longer tail.
Dark brown above, with the pale rump. A separate flight pattern was not named.
Yellow-buff underparts. The underwing was not named.

calls.description: A hissing kuss, kuss, higher-pitched than the Red-billed Oxpecker. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade B from Sabie Game Reserve. No playable grade A was listed.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it a fairly common, localised resident. Chick down beyond the duller plumage and dusky bill is not described, and there is no flight photograph. The call is grade B.
